title: What If the Year Had 13 Months? Kodak Lived That Way for 61 Years

scenes.text: What if the year had thirteen months? One company actually did it, for sixty-one years.
Thirteen months of exactly twenty-eight days. Every month starts on a Sunday. The new month, Sol, sits between June and July.
That's 364 days. The leftover day, Year Day, belongs to no week and no month. A holiday outside time.
In 1928 George Eastman switched all of Kodak to it. Every quarter exactly ninety-one days. They kept it until 1989.
The League of Nations rated it the best of 130 proposals. Then religious leaders objected: a day outside the week breaks the Sabbath cycle.
And one more problem. The 13th of every month lands on the same weekday. A Friday. Thirteen Friday the 13ths a year.

description:
What if the year had 13 months of 28 days? Moses Cotsworth proposed exactly that in 1902, and George Eastman ran the Kodak company on it from 1928 to 1989.
Every month starts on a Sunday, the extra month Sol sits between June and July, and a Year Day outside any week makes up the 365th day. The League of Nations rated it the best of 130 proposals, but religious objections to a day outside the seven-day week killed it, and every month would contain a Friday the 13th.
What should we run through next?
